source.title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems

accepted.question_text: For equivariant map algebras M(X, a)^Gamma, where X is an affine scheme, a is a finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field, and Gamma acts on X and a by automorphisms, what can be said about the theory when Gamma is replaced by a more general group, such as an algebraic group acting completely reducibly on the coordinate algebra A of X and on a? In particular, how can one classify the irreducible finite-dimensional representations of the resulting equivariant map algebras?

evidence.quote: The first step in the study of the resulting EMAs would be to classify their irreducible finite-dimensional representations.

accepted.question_text: For equivariant map algebras, how can the representation theory be developed when the target algebra is not one of the finite-dimensional Lie or associative targets usually considered, but instead is a target such as a Kac-Moody algebra, the Heisenberg algebra, an alternative algebra, or a Jordan algebra, provided that the chosen target has a well-defined notion of representations?

evidence.quote: There are many possible choices for the “target” algebra g for which the resulting EMA has not been studied.

accepted.question_text: How can equivariant map superalgebras be generalized by allowing more general Lie superalgebras as targets, replacing the coordinate algebra A by a supercommutative algebra so that X becomes a superscheme, and replacing Gamma by a Z2-graded group?

evidence.quote: The equivariant map superalgebra setting of [Sav] can be naturally generalized.

accepted.question_text: What is the appropriate analytic version of equivariant map algebra theory when the algebraic setting is replaced by, for example, a Banach manifold X, a Banach algebra a, and equivariant differentiable maps from X to a?

evidence.quote: Another interesting problem is to replace the algebraic setting by an analytic one.

accepted.question_text: How can equivariant map algebras be characterized up to isomorphism in general? More specifically, can the known isomorphism results and cohomological invariants for loop algebras and certain two-variable multiloop cases be generalized to the multiloop case and then to more general equivariant map algebras M(X, a)^Gamma?

evidence.quote: Characterizing EMAs up to isomorphism is one of the fundamental problems in the theory of EMAs.

accepted.question_text: How can one determine the automorphism groups of equivariant map algebras, beyond the cases where automorphism groups are already known for untwisted algebras, twisted loop algebras, or multiloop algebras?

evidence.quote: Related to the problem of characterizing EMAs up to isomorphism, is the question of determining the automorphism groups of EMAs.

accepted.question_text: For M = M(X, a)^Gamma with a a finite-dimensional associative algebra, how can one describe all indecomposable finite-dimensional M-modules and understand the block decomposition of the finite-dimensional module category, going beyond the known classification of irreducible objects?

evidence.quote: Ideally, one would like to describe all of the indecomposable finite-dimensional modules and understand the block decomposition of this category.

accepted.question_text: When the target algebra a is an associative bialgebra, how should the multi-orbit evaluation representations that arise from the comultiplication on a be understood?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to understand these representations.

accepted.question_text: For equivariant map Lie algebras M = M(X, g)^Gamma with g a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, how can higher Ext groups between finite-dimensional modules be computed, and how is the global dimension of the finite-dimensional module category related to the geometry of the scheme X?

evidence.quote: It is natural to try to compute higher Ext groups.
It would be particularly interesting to see how the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional modules is related to this geometry.

accepted.question_text: For equivariant map Lie algebras, how can the theory of global and local Weyl modules be extended so that results on lengths, dimensions, and characters of local Weyl modules, as well as BGG reciprocity, are available for more arbitrary equivariant map algebra settings?

evidence.quote: The study of (global and local) Weyl modules for EMAs is an active area of research.

accepted.question_text: For arbitrary equivariant map algebras, how can representation categories broader than finite-dimensional representations be developed, analogous to the categories studied for loop and current algebras, such as category O for central extensions of loop algebras, integrable highest weight representations, quasifinite representations with finite-dimensional weight spaces, or suitable generalizations of category O?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to study analogous categories in the more arbitrary EMA setting.

accepted.question_text: For an equivariant map Lie algebra M = M(X, g)^Gamma with g semisimple, how can the first cohomology group H1(M, V) be described for a general M-module V, and how can the homology groups H*(M, V) be determined?

evidence.quote: One can therefore expect that it should be possible to describe the first cohomology group H1(M, V ) for a general M-module V .
A related problem is to determine the homology groups H∗(M, V ).

accepted.question_text: For a perfect equivariant map Lie algebra M = (g tensor A)^Gamma, how is its universal central extension uce(M) related to the universal central extension uce(g tensor A) of the untwisted algebra? In particular, under what conditions does the natural expected formula uce((g tensor A)^Gamma) is isomorphic to uce(g tensor A)^Gamma hold?

evidence.quote: one would like to relate the universal central extension of a perfect equivariant map algebra
The formula one is aiming for is then very natural
